raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The KV Indexer answers the Router's prefix queries from process-local state, so an Indexer restart drops every placement and each deployment has to rebuild them from the workers' KV-event streams. Deployments that already run a [Tair KVCache Manager](https://github.com/alibaba/tair-kvcache) (KVCM) keep the same information there, and the manager already tracks reporter liveness and capacity eviction for them.

This adds a `tair_kvcache_kvcm` backend that keeps the Indexer's placement state in that manager's `MetaService` instead of the Indexer process. The Indexer becomes stateless: restarts no longer lose affinity, and the manager's own view of which reporter holds which block is the single source of truth for routing.

The component name and the clear mapping were coordinated with the Tair KVCache maintainers; the semantics this backend relies on were verified against the manager's implementation and its own tests.

## Modifications

- `KV_INDEXER_BACKEND=tair_kvcache_kvcm` selects `TairKVCacheIndexerBackend` (`experimental/sgl-router/sgl-kv-indexer/src/tair_kvcache_backend.rs`), configured through `KV_INDEXER_TAIR_KVCACHE_KVCM_*` environment variables.
- Apply batches translate to `ReportEvent` mutations: REPORT → `BLOCK_ADD` (one location spec per resident component), REVOKE → `BLOCK_DELETE`, `CLEAR_ALL_AT_TIER` → an empty `BLOCK_SNAPSHOT`, and the first batch per worker prepends `NODE_REGISTER`. Prefix queries translate to `GetHostCacheState` (`QT_PREFIX_MATCH`).
- Component-aware workers are excluded from answers rather than over-reported: the manager's whole-block answer cannot express SWA windows or MAMBA boundaries, so the backend fails closed exactly where the in-memory rule engine would.
- The clear-as-empty-snapshot semantics are documented in the README: the snapshot commits synchronously and fences the reporter's older locations behind strict visibility (scope: the whole reporter × storage channel, every medium); it travels alone in its request and in action order; snapshots are rate-limited per (instance, channel, reporter), 30s by default, and a flush inside that window is dropped with a warning instead of failing the batch.
- A vendored `tair_kvcache_meta_service.proto` (the manager's `MetaService`), a mock-based contract suite, and an env-gated live suite that runs the backend against a real manager (`tests/tair_kvcache_live/`).

## Accuracy Tests

Unit and contract suites need no external service:

```bash
cargo test -p sgl-kv-indexer
```

- `tests/tair_kvcache_contract.rs`: the backend against an in-process mock `MetaService` over real gRPC (translation both ways, KVCM acceptance rules, registration and error classification, clear retry/degrade paths), including one end-to-end pass behind the real `KVIndexer` service.
- `tests/tair_kvcache_live.rs` (`#[ignore]`d, real manager): 23 tests pinning the manager's observable behavior — accepted events and spec/URI rules, liveness reclamation and the `NODE_NOT_REGISTERED` self-heal, `snapshot_required`, medium filtering, and the clear (placements gone after a flush, a report after a clear landing on the fresh generation, and the rate-limit degradation path). Run them with `--ignored` after `python3 sgl-kv-indexer/tests/tair_kvcache_live/setup_tair_kvcache_manager.py start`; the README has the two commands.

End to end, on a 3-worker/3-bridge deployment with the Router on `cache_aware` + `--cache-prefix-provider indexer`: prefix answers matched the workers' own ZMQ event streams block for block under concurrent load and natural eviction, and the `flush_cache` wave went from 12/12 stale placements (before the empty-snapshot clear) to 0.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: this adds a storage backend to the Indexer's metadata path and does not change model execution. Query latency is bounded by `QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 50ms, half the Router-side prefix deadline).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to the [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Speed: not applicable, see above.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -249,6 +267,219 @@ Required or commonly used bridge variables:
   `KV_INDEXER_MAMBA_TIERS`: servable component tiers
 - `KV_INDEXER_CACHE_SPEC_VERSION`: component-rule version, default `1`
 
+## The Tair KVCache backend
+
+`KV_INDEXER_BACKEND=tair_kvcache_kvcm` selects `TairKVCacheIndexerBackend`, which keeps
+placements in a [Tair KVCache Manager](https://github.com/alibaba/tair-kvcache)
+(KVCM) `MetaService` instead of the server process, over the vendored
+`proto/tair_kvcache_meta_service.proto` (`kv_cache_manager.proto.meta.MetaService`).
+
+### Prerequisites and setup
+
+The backend is compiled into `kv-indexer-server`; a KVCM is required only under
+`KV_INDEXER_BACKEND=tair_kvcache_kvcm`, built from `main` at `5246532b` or
+later, the commit that added `GetHostCacheState`. An older manager answers
+`UNIMPLEMENTED`.
+
+Build and start a single-node manager
+([deploy](https://github.com/alibaba/tair-kvcache/blob/main/docs/deploy/README.md)):
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/alibaba/tair-kvcache
+cd tair-kvcache
+bazelisk build //kv_cache_manager:kv_cache_manager_bin
+mkdir -p ~/kvcm
+./bazel-bin/kv_cache_manager/kv_cache_manager_bin \
+  --env=kvcm.service.rpc_port=50052 \
+  --env=kvcm.service.http_port=50053 \
+  --env=kvcm.service.admin_http_port=50054 \
+  --env=kvcm.registry_storage.uri=local://$HOME/kvcm/registry.json
+```
+
+`rpc_port` is the gRPC port `ENDPOINT` points at, `http_port` serves the
+`MetaService` HTTP endpoints used to verify below, and `admin_http_port` serves
+provisioning. `local://` keeps the registry in one JSON file whose parent
+directory must exist. A port already in use logs `bind port: ... Address already
+in use` and the manager runs on without it.
+
+Provision an event-report storage for each channel the backend reports on
+(`ST_EVENT_REPORT_L1P5` for the default `STORAGE_TYPE=l1p5`,
+`ST_EVENT_REPORT_L2` for `l2`):
+
+```bash
+curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:50054/api/addStorage -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
+  "trace_id": "indexer-setup",
+  "storage": {
+    "global_unique_name": "indexer_event_report_l1p5",
+    "storage_type": "ST_EVENT_REPORT_L1P5",
+    "event_report": {},
+    "check_storage_available_when_open": false
+  }
+}'
+```
+
+`event_report` is the oneof member that types the storage; without it the call
+fails `INVALID_ARGUMENT {storage_spec}`. `check_storage_available_when_open` is
+`false` because an event-report storage holds metadata and has no medium to open.
+
+Then an instance group whose `event_report_storage_candidates` lists that
+storage:
+
+```bash
+curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:50054/api/createInstanceGroup -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
+  "trace_id": "indexer-setup",
+  "instance_group": {
+    "name": "my-deployment-group",
+    "storage_candidates": ["data_plane_storage"],
+    "event_report_storage_candidates": ["indexer_event_report_l1p5"],
+    "global_quota_group_name": "default_quota_group",
+    "cache_config": {
+      "reclaim_strategy": {"storage_unique_name": "data_plane_storage"},
+      "data_storage_strategy": "CPS_PREFER_3FS",
+      "meta_indexer_config": {
+        "max_key_count": 1000000,
+        "mutex_shard_num": 16,
+        "meta_storage_backend_config": {"storage_type": "local"}
+      }
+    },
+    "version": 1
+  }
+}'
+```
+
+`storage_candidates` and `cache_config` describe the data-plane storage the group
+shares with the workers' connector: use the one your workers write to. When the
+group already exists, post the same body to `updateInstanceGroup` with
+`current_version` from `getInstanceGroup` and `version` one higher.
+
+Then the instance:
+
+```bash
+curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:50054/api/registerInstance -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
+  "trace_id": "indexer-setup",
+  "instance_group": "my-deployment-group",
+  "instance_id": "my-model-deployment",
+  "block_size": 128,
+  "model_deployment": {"model_name": "my-model", "dtype": "FP16"},
+  "location_spec_infos": [
+    {"name": "full", "size": 0},
+    {"name": "swa", "size": 0},
+    {"name": "mamba", "size": 0}
+  ],
+  "default_query_type": "QT_PREFIX_MATCH"
+}'
+```
+
+Skip this when the workers' connector registers the instance itself;
+`INSTANCE_ID` names that instance. With `AUTO_REGISTER=1` the server registers it
+instead.
+
+Verify the three objects:
+
+```bash
+curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:50054/api/healthy
+curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:50053/api/getInstanceInfo -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"trace_id":"verify","instance_id":"my-model-deployment"}'
+curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:50053/api/getHostCacheState -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"trace_id":"verify","instance_id":"my-model-deployment","storage_type":"ST_EVENT_REPORT_L1P5","query_type":"QT_PREFIX_MATCH","block_cache_keys":[0]}'
+```
+
+The first answers `OK`, the second echoes the group, the block size and the
+`full,swa,mamba` specs, and the third lists the reporter's `host_ip_port` once
+the server has reported.
+
+Then start the server against it:
+
+```bash
+KV_INDEXER_BACKEND=tair_kvcache_kvcm \
+KV_INDEXER_LISTEN_ADDR=127.0.0.1:50051 \
+KV_INDEXER_TAIR_KVCACHE_KVCM_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:50052 \
+KV_INDEXER_TAIR_KVCACHE_KVCM_INSTANCE_ID=my-model-deployment \
+  cargo run --release --bin kv-indexer-server
+```
+
+Both directions of the translation:
+
+- `ApplyExternalKvBatch` -> `ReportEvent`: the worker id becomes the reporter
+  id, REPORT becomes `BLOCK_ADD` (one spec per resident component; legacy whole
+  blocks report `full` alone), REVOKE becomes `BLOCK_DELETE` (a superset
+  removal), `CLEAR_ALL_AT_TIER` becomes an empty `BLOCK_SNAPSHOT` (see below),
+  and the first batch per worker prepends `NODE_REGISTER`. Heartbeats keep
+  reporters alive so liveness does not reclaim idle-but-cached workers.
+- `MatchExternalKvPrefix` -> `GetHostCacheState` (`QT_PREFIX_MATCH`): per host,
+  the longest contiguous prefix from block 0, the same quantity the in-memory
+  backend computes. Reporters map back through the address restated on every
+  apply batch; a worker with no address is excluded.
+
+Configuration (all under `KV_INDEXER_TAIR_KVCACHE_KVCM_`):
+
+- `ENDPOINT` and `INSTANCE_ID` (both required): the `MetaService` address and
+  the instance (one per routed model deployment).
+- `STORAGE_TYPE`: event-report channel the deployment provisioned, `l1p5`
+  (default) or `l2`. `REPORT_TIERS` (default `HBM`) lists the forwarded tiers.
+- `AUTO_REGISTER` (default `0`) with `INSTANCE_GROUP`, `BLOCK_SIZE`,
+  `MODEL_NAME`, `MODEL_DTYPE`: opt-in `RegisterInstance` before the first thing
+  this backend sends. It declares the `full,swa,mamba` spec names and restates
+  the fields the manager requires; a registration must match an existing
+  instance field for field, or it fails `DUPLICATE_ENTITY`.
+- `QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 50, half the Router-side deadline) and
+  `APPLY_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 5000, one budget per batch, registration included).
+- `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS` (default 30000; `0` disables heartbeats). Keep it well
+  below the manager's EventReport liveness `heartbeat_timeout_ms`, which defaults
+  to 30s: with the default storage spec, set `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS=10000`.
+
+Semantics and limitations:
+
+- Host-dram events are dropped by default (the connector manages those
+  placements through the data plane; double reporting would race eviction);
+  `REPORT_TIERS=HBM,DRAM` widens the set for routing-only deployments. A tier
+  outside HBM/DRAM (`SSD`) is not servable by the prefix rules: legacy workers
+  still report it, but every worker declaring a cache spec is excluded from
+  answers (warned at startup).
+- `CLEAR_ALL_AT_TIER` is applied as an **empty `BLOCK_SNAPSHOT`**, the one
+  primitive with clear semantics: it commits synchronously and fences the
+  reporter's older locations behind strict visibility, so the prefix answer
+  stops claiming them immediately. Its scope is the whole reporter × storage
+  channel across **every medium** (no tier granularity); it travels alone (the
+  manager rejects a snapshot mixed with deltas) and in its action order. It is
+  also rate-limited per (instance, channel, reporter), 30s by default: a flush
+  inside that window is dropped with a `WARN` (`flush dropped, placements stay`)
+  rather than failing the batch, which would cost the deltas riding with it. The
+  first flush switches a delta-only reporter to strict visibility (that is what
+  hides the pre-clear blocks), so the indexer must be the only writer of that
+  reporter's placements on that channel; a per-medium `CLEAR` remains a
+  manager-side ask.
+- The prefix answer is the legacy whole-block quantity, so a worker whose
+  `cache_spec` needs rules beyond it (an SWA window, a MAMBA boundary) or that
+  reports component detail not confirming `full` (including a zero mask inside a
+  component batch, which the bridge produces for mask-less blocks) is
+  **excluded entirely** (fail closed, logged once per worker): the answer stays
+  a lower bound instead of over-reporting. `MatchExternalKv` has no equivalent
+  and answers `UNIMPLEMENTED`; `GetExternalKvHitCounts` stays empty.
+- A worker id must not contain `#` (the location-id separator) and the instance
+  must declare the `full,swa,mamba` spec names: either mistake fails
+  `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and the bridge exits, the desired fail-fast.
+- The reporter->address map is process-local: after an indexer restart, prefix
+  answers stay empty until the next batch restates an address. Placements
+  survive; only the join is lost.
+- `snapshot_required` is advisory (a reporter with no committed snapshot
+  version, the normal state here), so the backend logs it once per lifecycle and
+  never sends a snapshot; until live blocks are re-reported the index
+  under-reports, which is the safe direction.
+- Reporter liveness is destructive: a silent reporter is marked unavailable
+  after the heartbeat timeout and its placements are *deleted* once the cleanup
+  grace passes. With liveness tighter than `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS` the beats
+  land on a tombstoned node, the blocks are swept, and prefix queries keep
+  answering "nothing here" — a silently empty index, not an error. Check those
+  two intervals together first when cache affinity looks broken. The next report
+  after such a cleanup fails `NODE_NOT_REGISTERED` and the retry re-registers,
+  but the reclaimed blocks stay gone until the worker re-reports them.
+- A `NODE_REGISTER` is resent whenever a report fails `NODE_NOT_REGISTERED` or
+  never succeeded (each heartbeat also re-registers in passing). Permanent
+  configuration faults (`INSTANCE_NOT_EXIST`, `UNSUPPORTED`,
+  `REACH_MAX_ENTITY_CAPACITY`, a mismatched registration) are
+  `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, which the bridge treats as fatal; transient failures
+  are `UNAVAILABLE` and the Router degrades to load-based routing.
+  `SERVER_NOT_LEADER` (HA) is `UNAVAILABLE`: no leader redirects are followed.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 The SGLang Authors
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Bring up a real Tair KVCache Manager (KVCM) for `tests/tair_kvcache_live.rs`.
+
+The Tair KVCache backend of the KV Indexer has no in-repo server to talk to; this
+script starts one from a source build and provisions the event-report resources
+the backend needs (event-report storages, an instance group listing them, a
+registered instance). It is the reproducible half of the live integration:
+`tests/tair_kvcache_live.rs` asserts behavior, this script only allocates processes and
+configuration.
+
+    # once, in the Tair KVCache checkout
+    bazelisk build //kv_cache_manager:kv_cache_manager_bin
+
+    # --manager-repo is where the relative default --binary lives (or set
+    # TAIR_KVCACHE_MANAGER_REPO); an absolute --binary needs neither.
+    python3 tests/tair_kvcache_live/setup_tair_kvcache_manager.py start \\
+        --workdir /tmp/tair_kvcache-live --manager-repo <tair-kvcache checkout>
+    source /tmp/tair_kvcache-live/tair_kvcache_live.env
+    cargo test -p sgl-kv-indexer --test tair_kvcache_live -- --ignored
+    python3 tests/tair_kvcache_live/setup_tair_kvcache_manager.py stop --workdir /tmp/tair_kvcache-live
+
+`start` is idempotent: an already running manager is left alone and the
+provisioning is re-applied. `config` re-applies provisioning only. `start`
+verifies the state file's pid is still the manager it started before reusing or
+signalling it, so a stale workdir (they live in `/tmp`, which survives reboots)
+cannot make `stop` take down an unrelated process; `status` reports that check
+too. If the binary moved, point at it with `--binary` (absolute, or relative
+to `--manager-repo`).
+
+The liveness knobs below are deliberately tight (2s timeout, 2s grace, 100ms
+check interval) so the reclamation tests finish in seconds; a production
+deployment sets them to values an order of magnitude larger and the backend
+heartbeats once every 30s. Tests therefore configure their own heartbeat
+cadence explicitly.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import shlex
+import signal
+import socket
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import time
+from typing import Any, Dict, Optional
+
+import requests
+
+# --- Provisioning constants ------------------------------------------------
+
+INSTANCE_GROUP = "sgl_kv_indexer_live_group"
+INSTANCE_ID = "sgl_kv_indexer_live_instance"
+STORAGE_L1P5 = "sgl_kv_indexer_live_event_report_l1p5"
+STORAGE_L2 = "sgl_kv_indexer_live_event_report_l2"
+# The backend reports one spec per resident component under these names; an
+# instance that does not declare them fails every BLOCK_ADD.
+SPEC_NAMES = ("full", "swa", "mamba")
+BLOCK_SIZE = 128
+# Tair KVCache requires a model deployment on every RegisterInstance. Every field but
+# the name and dtype keeps its Tair KVCache default, which is what `TairKVCacheAutoRegister`
+# sends, so a backend that auto-registers this same instance is idempotent.
+MODEL_NAME = "sgl-kv-indexer-live"
+MODEL_DTYPE = "FP16"
+# Must match what `TairKVCacheAutoRegister` sends, otherwise re-registration of this
+# instance fails with DUPLICATE_ENTITY (Tair KVCache compares every field).
+DEFAULT_QUERY_TYPE = "QT_PREFIX_MATCH"
+
+LIVENESS = {
+    "heartbeat_timeout_ms": 2000,
+    "cleanup_grace_ms": 2000,
+    "liveness_check_interval_ms": 100,
+}
+
+DEFAULT_BINARY = "bazel-bin/kv_cache_manager/kv_cache_manager_bin"
+# No checkout is assumed: a relative DEFAULT_BINARY needs one, and the error in
+# `resolve_binary` says how to point at it (flag or environment).
+DEFAULT_MANAGER_REPO = os.environ.get("TAIR_KVCACHE_MANAGER_REPO", "")
+STATE_FILE = "tair_kvcache_live.json"
+ENV_FILE = "tair_kvcache_live.env"
+REGISTRY_FILE = "registry.json"
+
+
+class SetupError(RuntimeError):
+    pass
+
+
+# --- Process management ----------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def free_port() -> int:
+    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as sock:
+        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        return sock.getsockname()[1]
+
+
+def free_ports(count: int) -> list:
+    """Distinct free ports: four independent bind-then-close calls can hand back
+    the same number, and a colliding set only shows up as a startup timeout."""
+    ports = set()
+    while len(ports) < count:
+        ports.add(free_port())
+    return sorted(ports)
+
+
+def process_identity(pid: int) -> Dict[str, str]:
+    """What `/proc` says the pid is right now, for the checks below."""
+    identity = {"exe": "", "cmdline": ""}
+    try:
+        identity["exe"] = os.path.realpath(f"/proc/{pid}/exe")
+    except OSError:
+        pass
+    try:
+        with open(f"/proc/{pid}/cmdline", "rb") as handle:
+            identity["cmdline"] = (
+                handle.read().replace(b"\0", b" ").decode(errors="replace").strip()
+            )
+    except OSError:
+        pass
+    return identity
+
+
+def registry_uri(state: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+    """The registry URI every manager of this workdir is started with."""
+    return f"local://{os.path.join(state.get('workdir', ''), REGISTRY_FILE)}"
+
+
+def is_our_manager(state: Dict[str, Any], pid: int) -> bool:
+    """Whether `pid` is the manager this state file started.
+
+    State files live in workdirs under /tmp, which survive reboots, and pids are
+    reused: signalling on the strength of a stale file would take down an
+    unrelated process. The discriminator is the workdir-scoped registry URI in
+    the cmdline, because `/proc/<pid>/exe` is neither exact nor tolerant: another
+    manager from the same binary (routinely running on this host) reads as ours,
+    while a wrapper script or a renamed copy reads as a stranger we then refuse
+    to stop.
+    """
+    return (
+        bool(state.get("workdir"))
+        and registry_uri(state) in process_identity(pid)["cmdline"]
+    )
+
+
+def terminate(pid: int, timeout: float) -> bool:
+    """SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after `timeout` seconds. True when it is gone.
+
+    A manager is started in its own session, so the signal goes to the process
+    group: a wrapper script that execs the manager (or spawns it) leaves children
+    in that group, and signalling only the recorded pid would orphan them.
+    """
+    try:
+        group = os.getpgid(pid)
+    except ProcessLookupError:
+        return True
+
+    def send(signum: int) -> bool:
+        try:
+            # Only ever a group the manager leads; signalling our own would be
+            # catastrophic, and a pid without its own session cannot be ours.
+            if group == pid:
+                os.killpg(group, signum)
+            else:
+                os.kill(pid, signum)
+            return True
+        except ProcessLookupError:
+            return False
+
+    if not send(signal.SIGTERM):
+        return True
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline and pid_alive(pid):
+        time.sleep(0.2)
+    if pid_alive(pid):
+        print(f"[setup] pid {pid} ignored SIGTERM; sending SIGKILL")
+        if not send(signal.SIGKILL):
+            return True
+        time.sleep(0.5)
+    return not pid_alive(pid)
+
+
+def state_path(workdir: str) -> str:
+    return os.path.join(workdir, STATE_FILE)
+
+
+def read_state(workdir: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
+    try:
+        with open(state_path(workdir)) as handle:
+            return json.load(handle)
+    except FileNotFoundError:
+        return None
+
+
+def write_state(workdir: str, state: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    with open(state_path(workdir), "w") as handle:
+        json.dump(state, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
+
+
+def pid_alive(pid: int) -> bool:
+    """False for a pid that is gone, and for a zombie: `kill(pid, 0)` succeeds on
+    a zombie, which would read as "still running" until its parent reaps it."""
+    try:
+        os.kill(pid, 0)
+    except ProcessLookupError:
+        return False
+    except PermissionError:
+        return True
+    try:
+        with open(f"/proc/{pid}/stat", "rb") as handle:
+            # "<pid> (<comm>) <state> ..."; comm may itself contain spaces and
+            # parentheses, so split on the last one.
+            state = handle.read().rsplit(b")", 1)[-1].split()
+        return not state or state[0] != b"Z"
+    except OSError:
+        return True
+
+
+def resolve_binary(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
+    binary = args.binary
+    if not os.path.isabs(binary):
+        if not args.manager_repo:
+            raise SetupError(
+                "a relative --binary needs the Tair KVCache checkout it lives in: pass "
+                "--manager-repo <tair-kvcache checkout> (or set TAIR_KVCACHE_MANAGER_REPO), "
+                "or pass an absolute --binary <path to kv_cache_manager_bin>"
+            )
+        binary = os.path.join(args.manager_repo, binary)
+    if not os.access(binary, os.X_OK):
+        raise SetupError(
+            f"Tair KVCache binary not found at {binary}; build it with "
+            f"`cd {args.manager_repo} && bazelisk build //kv_cache_manager:kv_cache_manager_bin`"
+        )
+    return binary
+
+
+def http_post(
+    url: str, payload: Dict[str, Any], timeout: float = 5.0
+) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    try:
+        response = requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=timeout)
+    except requests.RequestException as error:
+        raise SetupError(f"POST {url} failed: {error}") from error
+    if response.status_code != 200:
+        raise SetupError(
+            f"POST {url} returned HTTP {response.status_code}: {response.text[:400]}"
+        )
+    try:
+        return response.json()
+    except ValueError as error:
+        raise SetupError(
+            f"POST {url} returned non-JSON: {response.text[:400]}"
+        ) from error
+
+
+def status_code(body: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+    return str(body.get("header", {}).get("status", {}).get("code"))
+
+
+def status_message(body: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+    return str(body.get("header", {}).get("status", {}).get("message", ""))
+
+
+def api_post(url: str, payload: Dict[str, Any], accept=("OK",)) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    body = http_post(url, payload)
+    code = status_code(body)
+    if code not in accept:
+        raise SetupError(
+            f"POST {url} failed: code={code} message={status_message(body)} body={json.dumps(body)[:400]}"
+        )
+    return body
+
+
+def wait_ready(http_port: int, timeout: float) -> None:
+    """Polls the meta HTTP API; the gRPC service starts in the same process."""
+    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{http_port}/api/getClusterInfo"
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    last_error = "no attempt made"
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        try:
+            body = http_post(
+                url, {"trace_id": "sgl_kv_indexer_live_readiness"}, timeout=2.0
+            )
+            code = status_code(body)
+            if code in ("OK", "SERVER_NOT_LEADER"):
+                return
+            last_error = f"code={code} message={status_message(body)}"
+        except SetupError as error:
+            last_error = str(error)
+        time.sleep(0.2)
+    raise SetupError(
+        f"Tair KVCache did not become ready within {timeout:.0f}s: {last_error}"
+    )
+
+
+def start_once(args: argparse.Namespace) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """One attempt: spawn a manager on a fresh port set and wait for readiness."""
+    binary = resolve_binary(args)
+    rpc_port, http_port, admin_rpc_port, admin_http_port = free_ports(4)
+    registry = os.path.join(args.workdir, REGISTRY_FILE)
+    command = [
+        binary,
+        f"--env=kvcm.service.rpc_port={rpc_port}",
+        f"--env=kvcm.service.http_port={http_port}",
+        f"--env=kvcm.service.admin_rpc_port={admin_rpc_port}",
+        f"--env=kvcm.service.admin_http_port={admin_http_port}",
+        f"--env=kvcm.registry_storage.uri=local://{registry}",
+        "--env=kvcm.service.enable_debug_service=false",
+        "--env=kvcm.logger.log_level=4",
+    ]
+    print(f"[setup] starting {shlex.join(command)}")
+    with (
+        open(os.path.join(args.workdir, "stdout.log"), "ab") as stdout,
+        open(os.path.join(args.workdir, "stderr.log"), "ab") as stderr,
+    ):
+        process = subprocess.Popen(
+            command,
+            cwd=args.workdir,
+            stdout=stdout,
+            stderr=stderr,
+            start_new_session=True,
+        )
+    state = {
+        "binary": binary,
+        "pid": process.pid,
+        "rpc_port": rpc_port,
+        "http_port": http_port,
+        "admin_rpc_port": admin_rpc_port,
+        "admin_http_port": admin_http_port,
+        "workdir": args.workdir,
+        "instance_id": INSTANCE_ID,
+        "instance_group": INSTANCE_GROUP,
+    }
+    write_state(args.workdir, state)
+    try:
+        wait_ready(http_port, args.startup_timeout)
+    except SetupError as error:
+        # A manager that never became ready is still holding its ports and
+        # writing logs; leaving it behind turns one failed start into a leak.
+        tail(os.path.join(args.workdir, "stderr.log"))
+        reaped = terminate(process.pid, args.stop_timeout)
+        if reaped:
+            try:
+                # Reap our own child, so it cannot linger as a zombie.
+                process.wait(timeout=2)
+            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+                reaped = False
+        if reaped:
+            os.remove(state_path(args.workdir))
+            raise SetupError(
+                f"{error} (the manager never became ready; pid {process.pid} shut down)"
+            ) from error
+        raise SetupError(
+            f"{error} (pid {process.pid} survived shutdown and still holds "
+            f"ports {rpc_port}/{http_port}; `stop` will retry it)"
+        ) from error
+    print(
+        f"[setup] Tair KVCache ready: grpc=127.0.0.1:{rpc_port} http=127.0.0.1:{http_port}"
+    )
+    return state
+
+
+def start_manager(args: argparse.Namespace) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    os.makedirs(args.workdir, exist_ok=True)
+    existing = read_state(args.workdir)
+    if existing and pid_alive(int(existing["pid"])):
+        pid = int(existing["pid"])
+        if is_our_manager(existing, pid):
+            print(
+                f"[setup] Tair KVCache already running (pid={pid}, grpc=127.0.0.1:{existing['rpc_port']})"
+            )
+            return existing
+        # A reused pid would otherwise make `start` report "already running"
+        # and provision against ports this state file no longer owns.
+        print(
+            f"[setup] state file is stale: pid {pid} is "
+            f"{process_identity(pid)['exe'] or 'unknown'}, not the recorded manager"
+        )
+        os.remove(state_path(args.workdir))
+
+    last_error = None
+    for attempt in range(1, args.start_attempts + 1):
+        try:
+            return start_once(args)
+        except SetupError as error:
+            last_error = error
+            print(
+                f"[setup] start attempt {attempt}/{args.start_attempts} failed: {error}"
+            )
+    raise last_error
+
+
+def stop_manager(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
+    state = read_state(args.workdir)
+    if not state:
+        print(f"[setup] no state file in {args.workdir}; nothing to stop")
+        return 0
+    pid = int(state["pid"])
+    if not pid_alive(pid):
+        print(f"[setup] Tair KVCache (pid={pid}) is not running")
+        os.remove(state_path(args.workdir))
+        return 0
+    if not is_our_manager(state, pid):
+        identity = process_identity(pid)
+        raise SetupError(
+            f"pid {pid} is {identity['exe'] or 'unknown'} "
+            f"({identity['cmdline'] or 'cmdline unreadable'}), not the manager this state file "
+            f"started ({state.get('binary')}); refusing to signal it. "
+            f"The manager is gone or the pid was reused: remove {state_path(args.workdir)} and run `start`."
+        )
+    if not terminate(pid, args.stop_timeout):
+        raise SetupError(f"pid {pid} survived SIGKILL; check it manually")
+    print(f"[setup] Tair KVCache (pid={pid}) stopped")
+    os.remove(state_path(args.workdir))
+    return 0
+
+
+def tail(path: str, lines: int = 20) -> None:
+    try:
+        with open(path) as handle:
+            content = handle.readlines()[-lines:]
+    except OSError:
+        return
+    if content:
+        print(f"[setup] last lines of {path}:")
+        sys.stdout.writelines(content)
+
+
+# --- Provisioning ----------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def event_report_storage(name: str, storage_type: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    return {
+        "global_unique_name": name,
+        "storage_type": storage_type,
+        "event_report": LIVENESS,
+        # Event-report storages hold metadata only; there is no medium to open.
+        "check_storage_available_when_open": False,
+    }
+
+
+def instance_group() -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    return {
+        "name": INSTANCE_GROUP,
+        "storage_candidates": ["nfs_01"],
+        "global_quota_group_name": "default_quota_group",
+        "max_instance_count": 10000,
+        "quota": {
+            "capacity": 10737418240,
+            "quota_config": [{"storage_type": 4, "capacity": 10737418240}],
+        },
+        "cache_config": {
+            "reclaim_strategy": {
+                "storage_unique_name": "nfs_01",
+                "reclaim_policy": 1,
+                "trigger_strategy": {"used_size": 1073741824, "used_percentage": 0.8},
+                "trigger_period_seconds": 60,
+                "reclaim_step_size": 1073741824,
+                "reclaim_step_percentage": 10,
+            },
+            "data_storage_strategy": 2,
+            "meta_indexer_config": {
+                "max_key_count": 1000000,
+                "mutex_shard_num": 16,
+                "batch_key_size": 16,
+                "meta_storage_backend_config": {
+                    "storage_type": "local",
+                    "storage_uri": "",
+                },
+                "meta_cache_policy_config": {"type": "LRU", "capacity": 10000},
+            },
+        },
+        "event_report_storage_candidates": [STORAGE_L1P5, STORAGE_L2],
+        "version": 1,
+    }
+
+
+def instance_registration() -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    return {
+        "trace_id": "sgl_kv_indexer_live_register",
+        "instance_group": INSTANCE_GROUP,
+        "instance_id": INSTANCE_ID,
+        "block_size": BLOCK_SIZE,
+        "location_spec_infos": [{"name": name, "size": 0} for name in SPEC_NAMES],
+        "model_deployment": {"model_name": MODEL_NAME, "dtype": MODEL_DTYPE},
+        "default_query_type": DEFAULT_QUERY_TYPE,
+    }
+
+
+def provision(state: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    admin = f"http://127.0.0.1:{state['admin_http_port']}"
+    meta = f"http://127.0.0.1:{state['http_port']}"
+
+    existing_storages = {
+        storage["global_unique_name"]
+        for storage in api_post(
+            f"{admin}/api/listStorage", {"trace_id": "sgl_kv_indexer_live_list_storage"}
+        ).get("storage", [])
+    }
+    for name, storage_type in (
+        (STORAGE_L1P5, "ST_EVENT_REPORT_L1P5"),
+        (STORAGE_L2, "ST_EVENT_REPORT_L2"),
+    ):
+        storage = event_report_storage(name, storage_type)
+        if name not in existing_storages:
+            api_post(
+                f"{admin}/api/addStorage",
+                {"trace_id": f"sgl_kv_indexer_live_add_{name}", "storage": storage},
+            )
+        # updateStorage is remove + add, so it makes the liveness knobs
+        # authoritative on every run whether or not the storage already existed.
+        api_post(
+            f"{admin}/api/updateStorage",
+            {
+                "trace_id": f"sgl_kv_indexer_live_update_{name}",
+                "storage": storage,
+                "force_update": True,
+            },
+        )
+        print(
+            f"[setup] event-report storage {name} ({storage_type}) configured, liveness={LIVENESS}"
+        )
+
+    existing_groups = {
+        group["name"]
+        for group in api_post(
+            f"{admin}/api/listInstanceGroup",
+            {"trace_id": "sgl_kv_indexer_live_list_group"},
+        ).get("instance_group", [])
+    }
+    if INSTANCE_GROUP not in existing_groups:
+        api_post(
+            f"{admin}/api/createInstanceGroup",
+            {
+                "trace_id": "sgl_kv_indexer_live_create_group",
+                "instance_group": instance_group(),
+            },
+        )
+    print(f"[setup] instance group {INSTANCE_GROUP} configured")
+
+    api_post(
+        f"{meta}/api/registerInstance",
+        instance_registration(),
+        accept=("OK", "DUPLICATE_ENTITY"),
+    )
+    print(
+        f"[setup] instance {INSTANCE_ID} registered (specs={','.join(SPEC_NAMES)}, block_size={BLOCK_SIZE})"
+    )
+
+
+def write_env_file(workdir: str, state: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+    lines = [
+        "# Generated by sgl-kv-indexer tests/tair_kvcache_live/setup_tair_kvcache_manager.py",
+        f"export TAIR_KVCACHE_LIVE_WORKDIR={workdir}",
+        f"export TAIR_KVCACHE_LIVE_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:{state['rpc_port']}",
+        f"export TAIR_KVCACHE_LIVE_INSTANCE_ID={state['instance_id']}",
+        f"export TAIR_KVCACHE_LIVE_INSTANCE_GROUP={state['instance_group']}",
+        f"export TAIR_KVCACHE_LIVE_MODEL_NAME={MODEL_NAME}",
+        f"export TAIR_KVCACHE_LIVE_MODEL_DTYPE={MODEL_DTYPE}",
+        f"export TAIR_KVCACHE_LIVE_HTTP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:{state['http_port']}",
+        f"export TAIR_KVCACHE_LIVE_ADMIN_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:{state['admin_http_port']}",
+    ]
+    path = os.path.join(workdir, ENV_FILE)
+    with open(path, "w") as handle:
+        handle.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+    return path
+
+
+def print_instructions(state: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    path = write_env_file(state["workdir"], state)
+    print(f"\n[setup] environment written to {path}\n")
+    print(f"  source {path}")
+    print("  cd experimental/sgl-router")
+    print("  cargo test -p sgl-kv-indexer --test tair_kvcache_live -- --ignored")
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("command", choices=("start", "config", "stop", "status"))
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--workdir",
+        default="/tmp/tair_kvcache-live",
+        help="state, registry and logs live here",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--manager-repo",
+        default=DEFAULT_MANAGER_REPO,
+        help="Tair KVCache Manager checkout holding a relative --binary "
+        "(default: $TAIR_KVCACHE_MANAGER_REPO)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--binary",
+        default=DEFAULT_BINARY,
+        help="manager binary (relative to --manager-repo)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--startup-timeout",
+        type=float,
+        default=60.0,
+        help="seconds to wait for readiness",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--stop-timeout", type=float, default=15.0, help="seconds to wait for SIGTERM"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--start-attempts",
+        type=int,
+        default=2,
+        help="start attempts with a fresh port set; a stolen port is otherwise just a timeout",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    try:
+        if args.command == "start":
+            state = start_manager(args)
+            provision(state)
+            print_instructions(state)
+            return 0
+        if args.command == "config":
+            state = read_state(args.workdir)
+            if not state or not pid_alive(int(state["pid"])):
+                raise SetupError(
+                    f"Tair KVCache is not running in {args.workdir}; run `start` first"
+                )
+            provision(state)
+            print_instructions(state)
+            return 0
+        if args.command == "stop":
+            return stop_manager(args)
+        state = read_state(args.workdir)
+        if not state:
+            print(f"[setup] no Tair KVCache state in {args.workdir}")
+            return 1
+        pid = int(state["pid"])
+        alive = pid_alive(pid)
+        ours = alive and is_our_manager(state, pid)
+        print(
+            f"[setup] pid={pid} alive={alive} ours={ours} grpc=127.0.0.1:{state['rpc_port']} "
+            f"http=127.0.0.1:{state['http_port']} workdir={state['workdir']}"
+        )
+        if alive and not ours:
+            print(
+                f"[setup] pid {pid} is {process_identity(pid)['exe'] or 'unknown'}, not this state file's manager"
+            )
+        return 0 if ours else 1
+    except SetupError as error:
+        print(f"[setup] error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
